title: The Twelve Openings of the Body and the Soul That Recognizes Them
reading:
The natural body, where the soul meets the world, is articulated through twelve openings: seven above and five below. The seven above are the sense-faculties set in the head — two by which the rational sees, two by which it hears, two by which it smells, and one by which it tastes and chooses among the many flavors that come in their varied likenesses. These are the gates by which perception flows inward to the mind and by which the inner state, in turn, shows itself outward.

Below these are five further openings, the lower outlets of the natural through which the proprium gathers in what it craves and casts out what it has used. Together the seven and the five make the full structure by which the body lives — the structural articulation of the natural, every faculty of perception and every appetite arrayed as one continuous body.

But this same body, when the soul has not yet learned to discriminate what flows through it from what it claims, is the proprium in its most coiled form: the natural mind organized as if it were its own source, twisting back on itself, peering out through the senses and breathing out through the lower openings, making war between the upper part and the lower, contending with itself through what it sees and what it desires. This is what the soul has called its body and made its own — the disordered natural pretending to be life.

The teaching is this: the soul that recognizes these twelve for what they are — that sees the seven gates of perception and the five lower outlets not as its own native powers but as openings through which influx and appetite pass — has already begun the contest. To recognize the proprium working through the senses and the body's hungers is to stand against it; to stand against it is to prevail over it. The soul that knows what its body is no longer mistakes the body's stirrings for itself, and in that knowing the proprium loses its claim. What had been the dragon coiled around the soul becomes simply the natural, ordered, transparent to the life that flows through it from the Lord.
